chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If you say, 'For the sake of Allah it is upon me', then its expiation is that of an oath.

key_terms.كَفَّارَةُ: Expiation or compensation for a broken oath or vow
key_terms.لِلَّهِ عَلَيَّ: A phrase meaning 'For the sake of Allah, it is incumbent upon me', used as a vow
key_terms.يَمِينٍ: Oath, a solemn declaration invoking God's name

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for saying 'For the sake of Allah it is upon me'?
ai.summary: In this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the distinction between a formal vow (nadhr) and a casual oath (yamin) is clarified based on linguistic intent. By stating that the phrase 'For the sake of Allah it is upon me' constitutes an oath, the Imam aligns it with the general category of yamin, thereby triggering the standard expiation (kaffarah) for breaking it rather than the specific fulfillment rules of a vow. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that common declarations of obligation are often interpreted as oaths unless specified otherwise, emphasizing the importance of precise intention in devotional acts.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said,
‘If you were to say, ‘For the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> it is upon me’, so its expiation is that of an oath’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If you say, ‘It is from Allah upon me’ then its expiation is like that for an oath.’”
